bullets.text: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services over the internet.
Services include servers, storage, databases, software, and AI.
It allows renting computing resources on demand instead of owning physical hardware.
Analogy: paying for electricity consumed, not owning the power plant.
On-demand self-service: users access resources without human interaction.
Broad network access: services available over the internet from various devices.
Resource pooling: providers share resources across multiple customers securely.
Rapid elasticity: resources scale up or down quickly based on demand.
Measured service: usage is monitored and billed according to consumption.
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): delivers fundamental computing resources like VMs and storage (e.g., AWS EC2).
Platform as a Service (PaaS): provides infrastructure plus a development platform (e.g., Google App Engine).
Software as a Service (SaaS): delivers ready-to-use applications over the internet (e.g., Gmail, Zoom).
Public cloud: services shared by multiple organizations over the internet.
Private cloud: dedicated to a single organization for more control and security.
Hybrid cloud: combines public and private clouds for flexibility and security.
Community cloud: shared by organizations with common goals or requirements.
Advantages: reduced costs, improved scalability, enhanced flexibility, reliability, and innovation.
Challenges: security and privacy concerns due to remote data storage.
Challenges: potential downtime and issues with internet connectivity.
Challenges: compliance with industry regulations and vendor lock-in difficulties.
Challenges: performance concerns for high-speed or low-latency applications.
Data storage and backup (Google Drive, Dropbox).
Business collaboration (Slack, Microsoft Teams) and entertainment streaming (Netflix, Spotify).
Healthcare (electronic medical records, telemedicine) and education (Coursera, Google Classroom).
Research, large-scale data analysis, machine learning, and AI projects.
AI and Big Data analytics leverage cloud for high-performance computing.
Edge computing processes data closer to the source, reducing latency.
Multi-cloud strategies are gaining popularity to avoid vendor lock-in.
Serverless computing allows developers to focus solely on code.
Continued focus on security, compliance, and advanced encryption technologies.
Integration with AI, blockchain, and 5G will expand cloud capabilities.
